author: Subscriptor
body:
hey,

this thread is made for discussion about turning avicus fully 1.8 or leaving it both 1.7 and 1.8. here are the pros & cons:

Pros:
-Defense (putting buttons on floor which really helps to defend, its 1.8 only)
-No advantages, everybody in same version.
-Less lag (?) (I don't know, but I guess if they turn the server 1.8 it will cause less lag)
-Can use 1.8 blocks in maps & other 1.8 items
Cons:
-No blockhit
-Some people say 1.7 is less laggy

what do you think? which side do you support?

note: please, but please, keep this on topic because almost everything goes off topic.., also don't flame war.

Let's be honest here. Minecraft isn't the thing that has changed. It's us. I joined Minecraft in 1.2.5 and loved the hell out of it. Like...a lot. But, as soon as 1.6 came out the spark died. It didn't die because of the update, but because I now knew about everything. I could craft, smelt, fight, build, you name it. I had pretty much learned everything about Minecraft, and the updates kind of "overkilled" the feeling I had when I first had the game.

New players who got Minecraft in 1.8 probably feel just like you when you were in Alpha, Beta, or any of the earlier versions.

The point is, every single update that comes out will be hated by the older members because they lost their spark. They're never going to get that full feeling back.

Avicus turning 1.8 may be a good thing. It may be bad. We just have to wait and see.

replies.author: Zintenka
replies.body:
The points put forth here really point to the server upgrading to 1.8.

I'm tired of being limited to just 1.7 blocks. I wanna try out new block palettes. If the server fully upgraded to 1.8 then the lag that you guys complain so much about will be gone (mostly).

You guys say that you hate the lag yet you want the server to stay in 1.7...

Think about it... the server (The actual giant metal box) that hosts us is using more of its RAM and hardware as well as software to support two versions separately. That puts a lot of strain on the hardware and will cause it to just become more laggier and laggier.

But if we drop support for one and move over to the other, the lag will be (mostly) gone. Like seriously, i get 20FPS on avicus constantly and I have some really top specs. Meanwhile on most 1.8 servers i get above 20.

Its either we drop 1.8 and regress back to 1.7; which in my opinion is out of the question seeing that the player count will stagnate and  people will leave.

Or we drop 1.7 and upgrade to 1.8; this is the better option as people will adapt to 1.8 (Should've a year ago), less CPU strain on the server therefore less lag, the player count will potentially grow as newer players are looking for 1.8 servers.

Now, its up to Funky. Whether we stagnate then fall or we progress and rise.

replies.author: Upsoar
replies.body:
Avicus Must Switch To 1.8
The first release of 1.8 was on August 22, 2014. That is almost an entire year ago. While server cross-compatibility is nice and all, it should only be used during the transition period between updates. A month at the most. And yes, pvp in 1.8 works differently than pvp in 1.7. And someone using 1.7 would have an advantage to someone in 1.8. Switching to just 1.8 would eliminate this advantage. Anyone who complains that 1.8 is crap for pvp needs to get over it. It's Minecraft. It changes. Everyone has had almost an entire year to get accustomed to the 1.8 update, Avicus and a lot of other Minecraft servers have been babying everyone by keeping themselves 1.7 and 1.8 compatible. In addition, I think that having Avicus as a single-version server can/will fix a few bugs.
Other things to note:
-Complaining about block-hitting in 1.8? Get over it. It's still there, but sword blocking will be removed in 1.9.
-Complaining about knockback in 1.8? Knockback is different in 1.8. You've had plenty of time to adjust.                 -Complaining about lag in 1.8? One of the goals of the Mojang team for 1.8, was to have an update to improve performance. Go check you're settings. Disable "alternating blocks" and turn on VBOs.                                            -Complaining about how this update has ruined pvp? Hey, remember when they added the sprint key feature so you didn't have to double tap "w" to sprint? They said that update ruined pvp. And if we go even further back, remember when they added "sprinting" into the game? Guess what they said about it? This update ruined pvp.      Minecraft is a constantly changing game. You either adapt, or get left behind.                                                I apologize for the amount of salt in this post, but this is what I've been trying to talk about since 1.8 was released.

replies.author: Matic0B
replies.body:
Unless Avicus wants to die out it will have to update, its just a matter of time. If you want good PVP you should go a couple versions back not 1.7.

Pros of updating:
 - Constant features and support if anything goes wrong from Spigot or others
 - Staying up to date with new features in the game
 - Ability to grow (if the server runs multiple versions behind then people won't join because they would have to switch versions just for one server)

You might say you could support multiple versions at the same time but that is only good for when a new version comes out and thats it. The server would still run the earliest version (1.7 in this case) and users would not be able to experience any 1.8 things since its just a "hack" that lets 1.8 clients join.

You would limit map makers to use blocks and work on old version servers which in the long run, most of them will go away because they will want to use new blocks and wouldn't be bothered to switch versions. You are also limiting development because they work with older code with less support because they are not up to date. Mojang won't help you with a 1.7 server if the game is in 1.9 since the issues could already be fixed in 1.9.

And block hitting isn't gone.

In any way, if the server wants to grow it will have to stay up to date otherwise you might as well say RIP.

replies.author: Zintenka
replies.body:
This is a very base and rude comment.

It may "just be a block game" but do you actually know how much pressure voxels actual put onto CPU? Especially with all of that loading at the same time? Polygon-based games (For example, BF4, COD, and many more.) take less pressure on the system.

Think of the stuff you see on the screen as math equations. Polygons have less of them so therefore loading and FPS tend to be higher. However, a single landscape can contain hundreds, thousands, millions or billions of voxels. There is a lot more math involved with voxels and the CPU (The brain of the computer) is having a tough time trying to "answer" those questions and the lag seen by your computer is the CPU failing questions.

If minecraft crashes... well thats your CPU failing the test.

Speak carefully, there is a lot of science and math behind what you said. And an apology would do you well :T

@DaGoldBrick, I have intel i7 @2.93Ghz out of 3.33Ghz, 8GB of RAM (I can use all of it if i wanted to), Nvidia GPU. 1600x--I dont know resolution.

I can play 1440p60 videos on youtube without any problem. Even the higher one.

I can play Planetside 2 on medium at 40FPS with High being 30. Render distance set to 4,500 meters (4.5Km) so I guess that (Should) give you a look at the games I could play. I consider it pretty up there in today's gaming rigs.

Minecraft just gives me problems because the game itself isn't really optimized well (I think) so even high rigs can get a hassle from time to time.
